items.box: We are now in Finsbury Park to see a painting by Banksy, an internationally famous street artist. Banksy's artworks often carry social messages, and ⓐ<u>the green tree you see over there</u> is a good example. As you can see, he created a green tree ⓑ<u>by spray green paint</u> on a wall behind a leafless tree. Next to the tree, there is a person ⓒ<u>who is holding a sprayer</u>. What message does Banksy want to give us through this painting? In many people's opinion, he is telling us that nature is having a hard time. They think he wants us to take better care of it. The final stop of our tour today is Muswell Hill. Can't see any street artworks? Well, look down and look __(A)__. Do you see the little chewing gum paintings? They are by the artist Ben Wilson. Wilson is well known ⓓ<u>for painting pictures on gum which people drop it</u> on the street. His gum paintings often carry personal messages from people he meets on the street. __(B)__, the one over here is a happy birthday wish for a loved one. Wilson's gum paintings are tiny, but ⓔ<u>they give great pleasure to many people</u>.

lines: (A) We look down to find the chewing gum paintings in Muswell Hill.

items.box: Dr. Schofield's fight for Korean independence didn't stop even after the March 1st Movement. (A) He continued to write about the ⓐ[terrible / wonderful] situation in Korea for foreign newspapers. (B) He was under the watchful eye of the Japanese police, so he had to go back to Canada in 1920. (C) For the rest of his life, he worked hard to help Koreans, ⓑ[especially / hardly] poor students. (D) Dr. Schofield died in April 1970, and he was ⓒ[buried / born] in Seoul National Cemetery. (E)

items.stem: 윗글의 흐름상 다음 문장이 들어갈 가장 적절한 곳은?

I think you are <u>right</u>.

Everyone has the <u>right</u> to learn.

items.box:
Interviewer: Dr. Schofield, I hear you have a Korean name. Can you tell me about it?
Dr. Schofield: It's Seok Hopil. I love it because it sounds similar to my English name. Also, it has a good meaning.
Interviewer: I'd like to know why you helped the Korean independence movement.
Dr. Schofield: Well, I believe every country has the right to be independent.
Interviewer: What did you do after you returned to Korea in 1958?
Dr. Schofield: I worked hard to help Koreans, especially poor students.

because he believed every country has the right to be independent

items.box: Kim Mandeok was born in Jeju-do in 1739. She was a successful businesswoman. In 1795, she saw many people dying from hunger. So, she bought rice with all her money and gave it away to poor people. Her love for others was so ⓐ<u>selfless</u> that many people respected her. From her life, I learned that selfless love for others can make a big difference.

items.stem: 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ selfless의 영영풀이로 옳은 것은?

important in history
to come together in a group in one place
freedom from political control by other countries
to keep doing something without stopping
items.explain: selfless: 이타적인.

items.stem: 윗글의 Kim Mandeok과 같은 방식으로 다른 사람을 도운 사람은?

Kay Brown saw a homeless person in the subway and gave her own shoes to her.
Eliot Middleton spends his free time fixing old cars for people in need.

A pianist moved to a small town and taught music to children.
items.explain: 자기 것을 가난한 사람에게 나누어 주는 방식.
items.source: L6 Think and Write · Culture Project

items.box: Modern street art comes in many different forms, and it makes cities colorful and lively. Today, we are going to see some well-known street artworks in London. The place that we are going to visit is Shoreditch. Poor workers used to live in this area, but now it is one of the hippest areas in London. We can find so many great pieces of street art here. Do you see the painting over there? It is by the artist STIK. He is famous for using only lines and dots in his paintings of human bodies. According to STIK, the three figures represent the past, present, and future of Shoreditch. Which figure represents which? Well, look closely at the eyes of the three figures. They are just dots, but they will give you a clue.

items.stem: 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: STIK: An Artist Who Uses Only Lines and Dots
The History of Poor Workers in London
How to Draw Human Bodies
The Most Expensive Street Art in London
Why Street Art Is Dangerous
items.explain: Shoreditch 의 STIK 작품 소개.

items.stem: 윗글을 다음과 같이 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 ⓐ~ⓒ에 들어갈 말로 바르게 짝지어진 것은?

items.explain: used to live / lines and dots / eyes.

items.label: [17~18, 서답형1]
items.box: Do you know Seok Hopil? His English name was Frank W. Schofield, but he loved his Korean name. It sounded similar to his real name, and it also had a good meaning. Dr. Schofield was a Canadian doctor, and he first came to Korea in 1916 to teach medicine. (가) <u>그는 한국어로 가르치고 싶어서 곧바로 한국어를 배우기 시작했다.</u> (A) <u>He studied so hard that he was able to teach in Korean after only a few years.</u> He believed that every country has the right to be independent, so he helped the Korean independence movement.

items.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: Dr. Schofield didn't like his Korean name.
Seok Hopil sounded similar to his English name.

It took him more than ten years to teach in Korean.

items.explain: It sounded similar to his real name.

items.stem: 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)와 의미가 같은 것은?

He studied hard, but he wasn't able to teach in Korean after only a few years.

He was able to teach in Korean, so he studied hard after only a few years.
items.explain: so ~ that ... can = ~ enough to.

items.stem: 윗글의 밑줄 친 우리말 (가)를 <조건>에 맞춰 바르게 영작하시오.

items.stem: 다음 대화의 밑줄 친 Somi의 우리말을 <조건>에 맞춰 바르게 영작하시오.
